newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - May 20.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - May 20.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Burns Philp & Co Ltd said on Monday it would sell its herb and spice businesses in North America and Europe and return its focus to producing yeast. The group also announced the retirement of managing director Ian Clack and a A$24.4 million third quarter loss. It said it expected that its 1996/97 fourth quarter to end-June would be below the year-ago level.

Colonial Ltd made a strong debut on the Australian share market on Monday, its share price soaring on listing. Stags are expected to charge again on Tuesday, perhaps pushing prices down in a effort to take substantial profits above the A$3.10 institutional price and the A$2.60 retail price.

Newcrest Mining Ltd said early on Tuesday it would restructure its Telfer gold mine in Western Australia following a review of the operation. Newcrest said it would outsource non-core maintenance and service functions immediately, involving the retrenchment of 126 employees at Telfer and in support roles. It said it would report on the financial implications by the end of June.
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$19.03 (+0.341)

BHP released its monthly production report late on Monday, posting a 35 percent rise in copper concentrates in the 11 months to April 30, a six percent iron ore production rise, a nine percent coal production rise, a three percent steel despatches rise, a five percent LNG production fall and a two percent oil and condensate production rise.
